article: Humanitarian Intervention, Responsibility to Protect, and the Limits of Sovereignty

primary_sources.notes: Core Charter framework for sovereignty, non-intervention, use of force, Security Council authority, and collective security.

primary_sources.source_title: UN Charter Article 2(4): Prohibition on the threat or use of force
primary_sources.notes: Prohibits the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of any state.
Framework for Security Council action with respect to threats to peace, breaches of peace, and acts of aggression.
Canonical UN formulation of the responsibility to protect in paragraphs 138 and 139.

primary_sources.source_title: Security Council Resolution 1674 on Protection of Civilians in Armed Conflict
primary_sources.notes: Reaffirms provisions of the 2005 World Summit Outcome concerning responsibility to protect populations.
Authorizes measures to protect civilians in Libya and remains central to debates over R2P mandate discipline.

primary_sources.source_title: Definition of Aggression, General Assembly Resolution 3314
primary_sources.notes: Defines aggression and helps distinguish lawful security claims from unlawful force.

primary_sources.source_title: Military and Paramilitary Activities in and against Nicaragua
primary_sources.notes: Foundational ICJ authority on non-intervention, use of force, and limits on unilateral coercion.

primary_sources.source_title: Oil Platforms (Islamic Republic of Iran v. United States of America)
primary_sources.notes: Important ICJ treatment of self-defense, necessity, and proportionality.

primary_sources.source_title: Armed Activities on the Territory of the Congo
primary_sources.notes: Major ICJ authority on use of force, occupation, and violations of sovereignty.

primary_sources.source_title: United Nations Office on Genocide Prevention and the Responsibility to Protect
primary_sources.notes: Official UN resource explaining the responsibility to protect and its three pillars.
Secretary-General report elaborating the three-pillar strategy for implementing R2P.

r2p_pillars.description: The state has the primary responsibility to protect its populations from genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing, and crimes against humanity.
r2p_pillars.legal_function: Locates first responsibility in the territorial state.
r2p_pillars.limits: Can be invoked by abusive states rhetorically while failing in practice.

r2p_pillars.description: The international community should assist states in fulfilling protection responsibilities.
r2p_pillars.legal_function: Emphasizes prevention, capacity-building, diplomacy, and support.
r2p_pillars.limits: Often underfunded or neglected before crises escalate.

r2p_pillars.description: The international community should take timely and decisive collective action through the UN when national authorities manifestly fail.
r2p_pillars.legal_function: Links coercive responses to collective Charter processes.
r2p_pillars.limits: Does not create a general unilateral right of force.

humanitarian_intervention_framework.core_question: May force be used without host-state consent or Security Council authorization?
humanitarian_intervention_framework.lawyer_focus: Identify legal basis; distinguish moral claim from lawful authority.

humanitarian_intervention_framework.core_question: Did the Council authorize force or other coercive measures?
humanitarian_intervention_framework.lawyer_focus: Read operative paragraphs closely; identify objective, scope, duration, and reporting obligations.

humanitarian_intervention_framework.core_question: Can non-force tools protect populations before atrocity escalates?
humanitarian_intervention_framework.legal_risk: Over-securitization or underuse of peaceful tools.
humanitarian_intervention_framework.lawyer_focus: Map Pillars I and II before Pillar III coercive options.

humanitarian_intervention_framework.core_question: Does the mandate authorize protection of civilians?
humanitarian_intervention_framework.lawyer_focus: Separate protection measures from political objectives beyond authorization.

humanitarian_intervention_framework.core_question: Are genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing, or crimes against humanity implicated?
humanitarian_intervention_framework.lawyer_focus: Tie factual record to recognized atrocity categories and source evidence.

humanitarian_intervention_framework.core_question: Does the claim reproduce imperial or selective intervention patterns?
humanitarian_intervention_framework.lawyer_focus: Address double standards, colonial history, and equal application.

case_matrix.article_use: Illustrates limits of Security Council-centered protection.
